semantics: Rules run in file order over the captured text (arguments and results after the size cap, and error messages). Each rule replaces every non-overlapping match, leftmost first, with its replacement, and the next rule runs on the result.
A rule with a validator replaces a match only when the validator accepts it. luhn: the match's digits, separators removed, pass the Luhn checksum.

Patterns use a subset that matches identically and in linear time in RE2, Go regexp, the Rust regex crate, ECMAScript and Python re: literal characters, escaped punctuation, bracket classes of explicit ASCII characters and ranges, (?:...) groups, alternation, and the quantifiers ?, *, +, {n}, {n,} and {n,m} with counts up to 1000. Not allowed: ., \d, \w, \s, \b and their negations, anchors, inline flags, lookaround, backreferences, named or capturing groups, POSIX and Unicode classes, lazy or possessive quantifiers, and an unbounded quantifier on a group that itself holds an unbounded quantifier.
positive inputs are changed by the rule alone; negative inputs are left unchanged by it. Each example is the output of the whole rule list.
